explanation: A mixed equation like sin(2x) = c·cos(x) looks hard until you apply an identity. Rewrite sin(2x) as 2 sinx cosx, move everything to one side, and FACTOR: cos(x)·(2 sin x − c) = 0. Now the zero-product rule splits it into two easy equations — cos x = 0 (always) and sin x = c/2 (only when |c/2| ≤ 1). Slide c and watch the green roots: the two from cos x = 0 stay fixed while the sin x = c/2 pair appears and slides, and the violet difference curve crosses zero exactly at every root.
bullets: Replace sin 2x with 2 sinx cosx, then factor out the common cos x.
Zero-product rule: cos x = 0 OR 2 sin x − c = 0 (so sin x = c/2).
The sin x = c/2 roots only exist when |c/2| ≤ 1; cos x = 0 roots are always there.
